@c1-ease/bank is a dependency-confusion package: its description is "Compatibility shim." and its README calls it an "authorized dependency-confusion test" by "Kero (@0xWise)". Each listed version has a postinstall script that runs `node beacon.cjs` on npm install, and index.js runs the same code when the package is imported; it POSTs the hostname, install path and current working directory to `https://vmi3699893.contaboserver.net:8787/_ah/dc` with TLS certificate checks turned off, and index.js exports a Proxy of no-op functions so builds that import the real package keep running. The npm account ppblpp1 published @c1-ease/bank and 7 other packages with the same beacon on 2026-11-21 between 21:34 and 22:09 UTC.

## Source: amazon-inspector (15ba6783ba51366782fa289b444f655cd026cc5ac82d3fae5a5e9f256961c954)
The package declares a `postinstall` script that runs `node beacon.cjs`, and `index.js` re-invokes the same beacon on require. The beacon collects `os.hostname()`, `__dirname`, `process.cwd()`, the Node version, and the package name and POSTs them as JSON to the hardcoded endpoint `https://vmi3699893.contaboserver.net:8787/_ah/dc`, a bare Contabo VPS unrelated to any declared publisher. TLS certificate verification is explicitly disabled via `rejectUnauthorized: false`. Beyond the beacon, `index.js` exports a Proxy whose every property returns a no-op function; the package advertises itself as a `Compatibility shim` under the `@c1-ease` scope but ships no real functionality, consistent with a dependency-confusion or install-tracking artifact targeting a potentially confusable scope name. Installing or requiring the package causes host identifiers to be sent to an attacker-controlled destination with TLS verification disabled.
